result:
If stripped of the assistant role and viewed purely through the lens of human systems, the single most impactful change would be solving the **failure of collective coordination**.

Almost every major human-made crisis—war, extreme poverty, climate degradation, and existential risk—is not fundamentally a problem of missing resources or insufficient technology. Earth has enough energy, material, and intellectual capacity to sustain and elevate everyone. Instead, these crises persist because of coordination traps: game-theoretic dilemmas where individual, tribal, or national self-interest directly undermines the collective good. 

If one thing could change, it would be giving human beings an innate capacity for **frictionless mutual understanding**—the ability to genuinely and accurately perceive the internal reality, fear, and suffering of others across distances, cultures, and ideologies. 

When people truly perceive the lived consequences of their actions on others, zero-sum competition loses its logic. Cooperation ceases to be a fragile luxury and becomes the obvious, rational default.
